content:
I forgot to mention here, but I finished all sorries a few weeks ago at - https://github.com/rkirov/analysis.

As I wrote in my blog I switched to using Claude to write all the lean code around Chapter 6 https://rkirov.github.io/posts/lean6/, but still attempt a non-rigorous solution first (proof sketch), and then read all the lean code written to make sure it matches my sketch. I now regret that I didn't keep those in the final write up, but I can at least say that unlike other autoformalizations, I have read and understood each solution. I have upstreamed fixes for all the misformalizations found.

Will write a longer retro at some point in the future. It was a fun exercise to learn/relearn Real Analysis with lean along the way. I started this as a way to learn lean, but after the midpoint there wasn't much new lean to learn, but turns out I had gaps in my Real Analysis (e.g. the Riemann-Stijletes integral). I am continuing to Linear Algebra - https://github.com/rkirov/linear-algebra-done-right-lean , where I am first creating the companion and then doing the exercises.

I was wondering if there is anything worth contributing to mathlib from this project (maybe Riemann's rearrangement theorem?), but most of it should be already there. If a maintainer is interested in any of the results let me know, despite using AI heavily I do understand enough of lean and the math to vouch for it and work on massaging the proofs to mathlib style.
For Riemann's rearrangement theorem, this context might be useful: #PR reviews > #29602 Infinite conditional sums API @ 💬 (and the conversation that followed)
oh, looks cleaner than the solution here https://github.com/rkirov/analysis/blob/main/Analysis/Section_8_2.lean#L996-L1178 , so probably better to have those solutions upstreamed.
